Config.notes: Pixels per tile in the art

Line of sight: on | off. On = you only see creatures in your line of sight, indoor tiles (painted Roof in the map editor) stay under the roof until seen, and walls in your way drop to stubs. Off = everything is always shown.
How far (tiles) the player can see
Darkness (0-1) of the veil over tiles that are out of sight; 0 = no veil
How much darker (0-1) indoor tiles (painted Roof in the map editor) are drawn than outdoors, with everything standing in them; 0 = same as outdoors
While aiming (right mouse button held) the camera drifts toward the cursor by this share (0-1) of its distance from the screen centre; 0 = off
A wall that hides something you can see within this many tiles of you drops to a stub (the walls of the room you are in always do)
How out of focus the floors below you look when you stand upstairs, in pixels (0 = sharp, 0.6 = slight, 1.5 = strong)
on = class skills are in the game (Q/E ability boxes, the abilities list in the bag, the mana bar). Empty = switched off for now: players are shown none of it.
Terrain id left on the ground when a player takes up a floor they laid there. Empty = the terrain named Dirt, if there is one; none = the ground comes back as it was.
Opacity (0-1) of doors, windows and switches left standing on a wall that has dropped to a stub
Colour of the roof drawn over indoor tiles the player has never seen (a map can override it with its own roof_color in the editor Roof tab)
Tiles visible across (panoramic)
Tiles visible down
Where new characters appear
Time for one step, in milliseconds
TRUE: terrain running off the map edge gets no border there
How often the server writes players to the sheet (min 10). Level-ups, deaths and map changes are written at once.
How often an idle game asks the server what changed
Class used when none is chosen
Share of gold lost on death (0.1 = 10%)
Minimum time between basic attacks
Base chance to pick a lock (plus the class bonus, minus the lock difficulty)
Chance a lockpick breaks on a failed attempt
Hunger points lost per minute (0-100 scale; 0 = off)
Thirst points lost per minute (0 = off)
HP lost per tick while hunger or thirst is at 0 (0 = off)
Seconds between starvation/dehydration ticks
Extra infection damage added each tick as it worsens
How long a ranged enemy's applied status lasts (e.g. poison spit)
How far a monster will chase a player who shot/hit it from beyond its aggro range before giving up
Paper-doll hair a new character starts with (a hair_*.png layer); blank = bald. Hidden when a helm is worn.
Starting hair colour: a hair_* ramp from Tint.TINTS (hair_black/dark/brown/auburn/ginger/blonde/grey/white)
Damage a hit does to walls and objects, as a share of the attacker's attack (a weapon's own structure_dmg wins)
A wall beaten below this share (0-1) of its health has holes: you can see and shoot through it, not walk through
off = inside a claimed base only its owner and members can damage things; on = anyone can (raids). Outside claims anyone can always damage what was built
How close (tiles) you must be to a crafting station to use its recipes
Seconds before a harvested object (a tree, a wreck) grows back; an object's own respawn_s wins
on | off: can players build (blueprints)?

What a player must have done before they can build at all: a condition list such as quest:my_quest_id (that quest handed in), quest_active:my_quest_id, flag:can_build or level:2. Empty = everyone can build from the start
What a player is told when they press B before building is unlocked. Empty = "You don't know how to build yet."
on | off: does water on raised ground fall down the cliff to its south by itself? Off = only the waterfalls placed by hand in the map editor
The standard waterfall strip (frames side by side, each four tiles wide). Empty = art/tilesets/waterfall_anim.png
Milliseconds each waterfall frame stays. Empty = 110
The most items that trees drop and ground grows may lie on one map at a time. Nothing more appears until some are picked up
How often (seconds) a map looks at a few of its trees and its grass for something to drop or grow. Empty = 10
How much time away (seconds) a map makes up for when a player returns to it. Empty = 1800 (half an hour)
How far (tiles) from yourself you can place a structure
A freshly placed frame has this share (0-1) of the finished health
Minimum time between two goes at building or repairing
A full repair costs this share (0-1) of the build cost
Taking something apart gives back this share (0-1) of its cost (less if it is damaged)
Most structures players can have built on one map
Most structures one player can have built on one map
How many base claims one player may hold (all maps together)
Most members the owner can add to one claim

on = a claim cannot be placed with any of the map's own doors, chests or teleports inside its radius; off = players may claim existing buildings (their authored doors and chests stay usable by everyone)
Extra object kinds, separated by commas (e.g. furniture, wreck). They appear in Objects → kind and in the Kinds tab, where you can give them properties. A kind the rules do not know behaves like deco

How many steps a player may take in one go before the referee makes them wait (walking speed itself is move_ms). Stops speed cheats; raise it only if honest players on slow connections get pulled back
Multi-storey maps: how many tiles further a player sees for each floor they are above the ground
How many tiles from a wall (or a pillar: an object with property support) a piece of roof or upstairs floor may be, counted through the roof already there. 0 = no rule.
How many empty storeys the game supplies above every map for players to build on (roofs, upper floors). 0 = only the floors made in the map editor.
Walker monsters with no player within this many tiles stand still and do not think
on = a walker with nothing alive to chase attacks what players built, when it sees it
How long a reload takes when the gun has no reload_ms of its own, in milliseconds (0 = at once)
The body under the gear of a male character (the same for every class)
The body under the gear of a female character (the same for every class)
How many cells the bag has (each holds one stack; an item stacks up to its stack_max)
Seconds a carcass lies before it rots away
How near a coop a tamed animal has to be to make it its home
How many eggs may lie around one coop before the hens stop laying
Thirst restored by one drink from a water source
Toxicity one drink from a water source adds (a terrain may set its own)
Toxicity points that wear off per minute
From this much toxicity (0-100) it costs health
HP lost per starve_tick_s while that sick (0 = off)
Quests every new character starts with, shown in a welcome window the first time they enter the game. One or more quest ids, separated by commas. Empty = none

Objects.name: Letter
Objects.properties: {"text": "A letter. The handwriting is hard to read."}

Objects.name: Tree
Objects.notes: Two tiles tall: trunk (blocks) + crown (drawn above characters)

Objects.name: Wall Torch
Objects.notes: Wall-mounted: paint it in the Objects layer and it snaps to the nearest wall edge; set the side/height in the inspector. Walkable so it doesn't block the floor.

Objects.name: Wall Switch
Objects.notes: Wall-mounted, interactable: stand in the cell it hangs in and use it. Link it to doors/levers like any switch.

Objects.name: Door
Objects.notes: Edge door: paint it onto a horizontal wall in the Objects layer. Closed = opaque + blocks the edge; open = a see-through, walk-through hole the shape of the sprite. Interact to toggle. Walkable (it sits on the wall line, not the tile).

Objects.name: Garage Door
Objects.notes: A 2-tile-wide edge door (width = 2). Spans and gates two wall edges; opens as one wide hole.

Objects.name: Workbench
Objects.notes: Crafting station: recipes with station = workbench can be made within reach of it

Objects.name: Rubble
Objects.notes: Left behind when a storage container is destroyed; holds what was in it

Quests.name: Getting around
Quests.text: Walk with [W] [A] [S] [D] or the arrow keys. You can also click a spot on the ground to walk there.
Quests.notes: Sample tutorial step 1 (Config start_quests). Tick "tutorial": it finishes by itself and its rewards start the next step. Put a GIF of the game in "image"

Quests.name: What you carry
Quests.text: Everything you pick up goes into your bag. Press [I] to open it, and [I] again to close it.
Quests.notes: Sample tutorial step 2: a step only the page can see (a window opened)

Quests.name: Hitting things
Quests.text: Stand next to something and [Left click] it to hit it: a creature, or a tree to bring it down for wood.
Quests.notes: Sample tutorial step 3: the last one starts the first real quest

Quests.name: You are finally awake
Quests.text: You open your eyes and take a deep breath. Nowhere around you seems familiar, and it is so quiet that it feels eerie. Your throat burns. You should have something to drink.
Quests.done_text: That is better. The burning eases, and you can think again. Somebody is standing a little way to the east.
Quests.notes: Sample: the starting quest (Config start_quests). No giver and no ender: it opens in a window when the character first enters the game, and when its objective is met a window shows the done text with a Claim button

Quests.name: Rat trouble
Quests.text: The rats are into everything. Kill three of them and I will make it worth your while.
Quests.progress_text: Three rats. They are not hard to find.
Quests.done_text: That is three fewer. Here, as promised.

Quests.name: Bone charms
Quests.text: One more thing. Bring me two bones. Do not ask what for.
Quests.progress_text: Two bones. Rats have them, like everything else.
Quests.notes: Sample: a bring-me quest that follows the first, with a choice of reward
